verdict.rationale: Orb documents day-based proration on plan changes, crediting the unused portion of the period. It also keeps a complete audit trail of plan assignments and lets you preview invoice impact before saving an edit. However, the evidence shows no detailed proration math, rounding rules, or line-item reconciliation, so the 'to the penny' auditable part is unproven. Missing for 10: documented proration formulas and rounding behavior, explicit partial-period charge line items for the new plan, evidence that invoice line items reconcile to the penny, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, mid-cycle upgrades and downgrades are prorated with documented, auditable math — credits, partial periods, and invoice line items that reconcile to the penny

citations.quote: Orb will credit the customer an amount corresponding to the portion of the time period that was left unused using day-based proration.
Orb maintains a complete audit trail of every plan assignment.
Preview the billing and invoice impact before you save, so you can confirm how charges and invoices will look.
